kind: cross-validation against a mature open-source implementation (XVAL)

decision.question: Does TensorLBM's slab periodic-halo exchange (triton_fused_distributed) implement the *same* periodic-halo semantics as haimingz/vivsim's jax.lax.ppermute ring exchange, and which parts of the OSS 做法 are safe to port?
alternatives: H1: our halo is semantically equivalent to the OSS 做法 (error vs single-domain ground truth ~ machine epsilon) => nothing to port, OSS becomes a permanent cross-check reference.
H2: our halo differs from the OSS 做法 => quantify the divergence, keep ours if ours matches the ground truth, and record the OSS 做法's deviation as a porting caveat (never copy verbatim).
H3: both differ from the single-domain ground truth => our halo is defective (defect, not a porting question).
decision.rule: H1 is accepted iff (i) our arm reproduces the single-domain ground truth with rel-L2 error < 1e-12 (float64, no fp16 wire) AND (ii) the semantically-corrected OSS reference (REF-C) also matches the ground truth. H2 is accepted if REF-C matches but a literal port (REF-A) does not. H3 otherwise.

hypothesis.our_semantics: pull streaming with 2 ghost planes; lane set = {q : cz(q)=+1} sent to the +z neighbour and read as the -z ghost, {q : cz(q)=-1} sent to the -z neighbour and read as the +z ghost; periodic wrap via modulo neighbours; one batched 4-op P2P stage per step.
hypothesis.oss_semantics: jax.lax.ppermute ring with pair tables [(i,(i+1)%n)] / [((i+1)%n,i)]; per-axis one-ghost-layer exchange of the crossing lane sets (D2Q9 LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN); periodic wrap is folded into the pair tables (rank n-1 <-> 0).
hypothesis.equivalence_prediction: the same physical halo (crossing lanes only, periodic ring) but an independent implementation; expected agreement with the ground truth at float64 round-off.

arms.GT: single-domain periodic collide+stream (no decomposition) — the physical ground truth. For the 2D vivsim arm it is the upstream vivsim.lbm.basic.streaming() run on the whole domain; for the 3D arm it is a whole-domain torch pull-stream.
arms.REF-A: vendored vivsim.multidevice.stream_cross_devices, VERBATIM (39 lines, MIT), driven with SPMD-emulated lax.ppermute. Literal port.
arms.REF-B: same file with only the read-plane index corrected (plane 0 <-> plane -1); pair tables untouched.
arms.REF-C: same file with read planes corrected AND the x branch's pair tables aligned with the y branch (the semantically correct pull-streaming halo).
arms.GOT: TensorLBM DistributedTritonFusedSolver3D — the REAL constructor and the REAL _start_halo_exchange/_finalize_halo, run on CPU under gloo (2 / 4 ranks). Only two environment hooks are stubbed (CUDA gate + lattice-tensor factory) and the Triton streaming kernel is replaced by a CPU pull-stream that is itself validated against GT at world=1.
arms.CONTROL-LANE: GOT with the crossing lane tables swapped (+z / -z), a deliberate defect injection. Must fail. Proves the metric has teeth.

metrics.primary: rel_l2 = ||f_arm - f_GT||_2 / ||f_GT||_2 of the streamed field after N steps, per rank, gathered to the global grid then compared with GT.
metrics.unit_of_analysis: one (arm, decomposition, n_ranks, field case) configuration; 3 seeds for the random field case.
metrics.threshold: owner precision standard: error < 15% is acceptable, > 15% is not. Disclosed stricter in-house bound for a semantic-equivalence claim: rel_l2 < 1e-12 at float64 (i.e. the halo must be bit-exact, not merely <15%).

repetitions.physical_case: 3D Taylor-Green vortex, 40 steps, tau=0.6 (nu=0.0333), reported as kinetic-energy trajectory + rel_l2 vs GT
repetitions.rationale: the quantity of interest is a deterministic, non-statistical data-movement equivalence; 3 seeds only guard against a lucky symmetric initial field (the documented 'symmetric field hides lane errors' trap).

controlled: initial field (identical bytes on every arm)
dtype float64 (fp16 wire only in the marked sub-arm)
changed: halo convention (REF-A / REF-B / REF-C / GOT / CONTROL-LANE)
decomposition axis (x / y for the 2D arm; z for the D3Q19 arm)
confounders_controlled: streaming-kernel identity: GOT uses the same CPU pull-stream as its own GT at world=1 (checked), collision is one shared elementwise function on every arm
rank-block size: every configuration divides the axis evenly (both implementations require it)
initial-field aliasing: buffers are deep-copied per rank

analysis.aggregation: per-configuration error, no averaging across arms; mean±spread over the 3 seeds and the 2 rank counts
analysis.outliers: none discarded; the CONTROLE-LANE arm is expected to be a large outlier and is reported as the sensitivity floor
analysis.missing_data: if gloo P2P is unavailable the GOT arm reports as SKIPPED (honest), never as 0 error
analysis.predeclared_stop: stop and report honest-FAIL if the GOT arm cannot be executed at all (no code path, no glue) — do not substitute a re-typed re-implementation for it

environment.host: loong64 control-plane container, CPU only (torch.cuda.is_available() == False)
environment.jax: not installed (no loongarch64 jaxlib wheel) -> lax.ppermute emulated; the emulation semantics are stated in jax_shim.py and validated against the real distributed data movement of the GOT arm (identical ring result)

deliverables: REPORT.md (six sections + OSS-vs-ours difference list + porting trade-offs)
falsification: the harness is falsified if CONTROL-LANE (a one-line lane-table swap) does NOT produce a large error while GT/GOT agree exactly.
